title: AI Red Teaming Agent: Azure AI Foundry — Nagkumar Arkalgud & Keiji Kanazawa, Microsoft
talk_summary: Microsoft presents an AI red teaming agent built on the open-source PyRIT package, exposed via an Azure AI Foundry SDK and dashboard, that runs automated attack scans (risk categories, attack strategies like Base64/Caesar/reversal, composed converters) against a target app or raw model and reports attack success rates. The broader framing is a process: map risks, apply guardrails, then evaluate with red teaming plus quality and safety evaluators.

takeaways.what_they_do: Run a scripted scan that sends N objectives across risk categories using attack strategies (encoding, reversal, composed converters) at a target endpoint, then score which attacks succeeded and filter results.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the number of objectives is the number of questions that uh will be sent out to your application
takeaways.numbers: 160-objective scan on GPT-4o: 0 successes; on GPT-5.3: 5/40 hate-and-fairness successes; raw 4.1 without guardrails: 25% violence success

takeaways.technique: Attack-strategy converters as reusable test transforms
takeaways.what_they_do: Composable converters (Base64, Caesar, string reversal, URL-style) transform a seed harmful prompt before sending, and results are tagged by strategy so you can see which transform defeated the target.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can also compose an attack with two different strategies. So get a tense converted strategy and then do a URL style conversion on it

takeaways.what_they_do: Guardrails and evaluators are applied both to what goes into the model and what comes out, and the model itself stays raw with checks outside it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the guardrails are not in the model itself the model is still the raw model and the guardrails are actually kind of outside it

takeaways.technique: Scan the raw model separately from the app
takeaways.what_they_do: The same scan can target either the full application or the bare model config, isolating whether failures come from the model or the app layer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a lot of people might just be building models you don't even have an application you can directly call uh the scan against an open Azure OpenAI config

takeaways.technique: Red-team agent as a tool-callable plugin
takeaways.what_they_do: The red team capability is exposed as a plugin with functions an orchestrating agent can tool-call, so a chat agent can generate an attack prompt, send it to a target, and iterate interactively.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our red team plugin uh is something that our SDK exposes. It has all the functions that are needed uh for for an agent to tool call
